calendar.sources.footer: Calendars from a link or a CalDAV account. The server fetches them every hour, and the phone shows them in Calendar.
calendar.sources.info_label: About calendars fetched by the server
calendar.sources.info: Fetch Now on a link's page fetches it at once. Each phone gets the events in a calendar of its own, which the kid can't change; nothing more than 60 days old is sent. For a CalDAV account use an app password, not your usual password: iCloud makes one at account.apple.com, Fastmail and Nextcloud in their password and security settings. Google works only as a link: the calendar's secret address in iCal format. Nothing from the phone is written back - unless the kid's events are written to a CalDAV calendar (chosen under Calendar app).
calendar.sources.info_privacy: The server keeps the events (titles, descriptions, places, times) while the calendar is here, and sends them only to the phones that have it. Links and app passwords are stored encrypted and never shown again; a password goes only to the hosts on its account's page, and if the server answers from another host, fetching stops until you test again. An account is shared by every phone here, each getting only the calendars switched on on its page; one no phone uses is deleted, password and all, a day after it was last used. The events the kid adds on the phone stay on the phone - unless the kid's events are written to a CalDAV calendar.

device.about.crashes_footer: Vibb One restarts by itself after a crash. A report holds only where in the code it happened.
device.advanced.backup_on_sub: The phone turns it off at its next sync (Vibb One's Settings › Sync now). If it stays on, something on the phone keeps turning it on: report it.
device.advanced.restrictions_footer: A pause or the Parent PIN doesn't lift these.
device.advanced.restrictions_info: Block screenshots also stops screen recording and casting, and recent-apps previews go blank. Locate needs Keep location on. A reset from the recovery menu can't be blocked.
device.advanced.debugging_footer: Turn it off before you work on the phone with a computer.
device.advanced.debugging_info: While it is blocked, a computer can't repair the phone: if Vibb One breaks and can't reach this server, only a reset gets it back.
device.advanced.safe_boot_footer: Turned on with the first Child PIN: safe mode skips the lock.
device.advanced.safe_boot_info: Safe mode starts the phone without Vibb One, unfiltered (the restrictions above still apply). It repairs nothing, so blocking it costs nothing once Vibb One works on this phone.
device.advanced.backup_info: When on, Android may copy app data, calls, SMS and settings to Google. Vibb One keeps it off; there is no switch for it.
device.advanced.block_screens_footer: Turn it off only if something breaks.
device.advanced.block_screens_info: Screens of apps that aren't allowed never open, even from an allowed app. The Play Store stays paused, except in install mode and at night for updates.
device.advanced.fence_sub: Hides Android's home screen while Vibb One updates.
device.advanced.notification_filter_sub: Removes notifications that open blocked screens.
device.advanced.boot_cover_sub: Shows the Vibb logo while the phone starts.
device.advanced.updates_footer: Vibb One installs its own updates at night, with the screen off.
device.advanced.updates_info: Test Update fence and Boot cover (from the next restart) on this phone model first. The filter keeps allowed apps, calls, alarms and emergency alerts, and never reads a notification's text.

device.advanced.connection_footer: A new code reconnects the phone after a reset, replacing its current connection.
device.advanced.remove_confirm: Remove {name}? Its settings and history are deleted, and it can't reach this server any more. This can't be undone.

device.apps.downloads_info: Vibb One's own updates wait up to 3 days for Wi-Fi, then take any network. Nothing downloads while roaming.

device.lock.used_offline_sub: The time lock was lifted with it since the phone's last check-in.
